questions.topic: Specialised weeks — a NBFC and a PSU
o: Independent recompute from the overdue data: run the 90-day trigger yourself; the certificate is a representation, not evidence
questions.why: Classification is an output of the ageing; testing it from the ledger is the only route to substance (the certificate is management's assertion on the very matter under audit — a classic self-validating control to distrust in banks/NBFCs).

questions.topic: Specialised weeks — a NBFC and a PSU
o: Accept the classification at restructure date
Test the qualifying criteria were met AND whether monitoring-period breaches require reversion to a higher grade — the provision step-up follows the reversion
questions.why: Restructured accounts must meet the framework's conditions to earn standard treatment (and the monitoring-period logic: default during it = back to classification with higher provisioning); a 'once restructured, forever standard' book is a provision hole — the 90-day population is the test target.

questions.topic: Specialised weeks — a NBFC and a PSU
o: Beyond the FS opinion: the C&AG directions may require the auditor to report on delays as an additional matter (economy/propriety lens) — so the observation travels into the directions-based report section, not only the private letter
questions.why: In PSU audits the directions are the mechanism: compliance with administrative approvals, utilisation of grants/loans, and the economy/efficiency view can be part of the REPORT itself — the delay is a performance question with a reporting channel the private-sector auditor doesn't have.

questions.topic: Specialised weeks — a NBFC and a PSU
questions.q: If File B's project used a grant for a different purpose:
o: A specified-matter report item: utilisation of grants/devolved funds is the classic additional-matter category — quantify and name the deviation in the directed matters, since it also has accounting (income/liability) and propriety implications
questions.why: Misuse of earmarked grants is BOTH a financial-statement issue (the recognition of a liability to refund) and a propriety matter under the directions — the answer names the dual effect; the auditor books the liability AND reports the deviation.

questions.topic: Specialised weeks — a NBFC and a PSU
questions.q: What the partner must not do with the two files:
o: Let the NBFC's 'trust the certificate' habit leak into the PSU's grant testing — each file has its own evidence rules; also, never swap the team across independence lines
questions.why: The cross-file contamination risk is real (method laziness), and the ethics line is independence (partner on both is fine ONLY where no relationships cross); the 'evidence rules are file-specific' discipline is the audit-quality point.

questions.q: Under RBI prudential norms as applied in bank audits, a standard asset becomes an NPA when interest/principal remains overdue for more than:
questions.why: 90 days overdue ⇒ NPA classification (sub-standard at inception, then further categories with ageing); the rule is a core knowledge item for the bank-audit chapter and an audit-procedure hook (test the overdue ageing, not the management certificate).

mem.tip: A loan's life support runs on days, not optimism.

questions.q: A service organisation's controls are tested by the user auditor using the carve-out method when:
o: They are included in the service auditor's report and tested by it
The service auditor's report EXCLUDES certain controls, so the user auditor must perform procedures on them directly (or by other means)
No reliance is placed on the service organisation
The user entity performs all its own processing
questions.why: Under SA 402, the service auditor's report follows the included (carve-in) or excluded (carve-out) approach; where controls relevant to user entities are carved OUT, the user auditor cannot rely on the report for them and must test or obtain evidence by other means.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — read the service report's 'included/excluded' scope before trusting the opinion Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: The method names what the report covers — read the caption before the conclusion.

questions.q: Under the framework for bank branch audits, concurrent audit is oriented towards:
o: Verifying financial statements of the bank
Frequent internal checks on branch transactions at an early stage for compliance and risk rectification
questions.why: Concurrent (and risk-based) internal systems and controls audits are an EARLY-warning internal layer at branches — a supplement to, not a substitute for, the statutory audit; understanding their reliance informs audit coverage decisions (SA 610 thinking applied to internal-audit-style mechanisms).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — early-warning layer: internal, periodic, not an opinion Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Repetition is a remedy in a bank's audit model.

questions.q: A Type 2 service organisation report covers:
o: Design AND operating effectiveness over a specified PERIOD — gaps from the period end to the audit year-end need roll-forward work
questions.why: The '2' is the operations-over-a-period version; mismatched dates mean the user auditor fills the gap.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the calendar matters as much as the caption Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Reports expire like milk on the client's dates.

questions.q: A cost audit (where ordered under the Companies Act) is conducted under:
o: The SAs by analogy and the cost audit rules/CASB standards
questions.why: Cost audits have their own statutory track (Section 148 + rules; CASB standards) with a specified scope of cost records and reporting to the board/regulator — the FS auditor reads the report for inventory and costing consistency, they don't share an opinion.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — two audit regimes, one warehouse AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Cost audit counts the rupees in the process, not on the page.

questions.q: A trust audit of a charitable entity pays special attention to:
o: Application of funds to objects, 80G/12A compliance, related-party use, and the trust deed's constraints
questions.why: Non-profit audits pivot on application-of-income tests (are outgoings for the objects?), deed compliance, and the abuse routes (loans to trustees' entities, cash spending caps) — the standard profit lens misses the whole risk book.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — where the money went matters more than the surplus Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: A charity's P&L is a receipt list for the mission.

questions.q: A material arbitration award against the client received just before year-end is:
o: Evaluated as a legal claim (accrue if present obligation with probable outflow; disclose in contingencies if not accrued), and discussed with TCWG
Only disclosed in the audit report
questions.why: Awards crystallise contingent liabilities: the accrual/disclosure test applies from the date the obligation and estimate are evident — the lawyer's letter + the award's date decide the reporting year, not the enforcement.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the award is the event, not the recovery Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: A losing verdict is a debt with a stamp.
